core_obligations: Stalk computation (proof lines 19013-19025): the canonical map is checked on stalks, and since derived tensor products commute with pullback one has (E tensor^L_Z f^{-1}K)_x = E_x tensor^L_Z K_y for the image y of x; since Z has global dimension one this complex vanishes in degrees below -1 + a + b when H^i(E) = 0 for i >= a and H^j(K) = 0 for j >= b.

Torsion of the coefficients (proof lines 19026-19038): because each H^i(E) is a torsion abelian sheaf, the cohomology sheaves of E tensor^L_Z f^{-1}K are torsion as well, as the displayed computation with Q shows; this is what allows the pull-out lemma to be applied over the ring of integers.

Conclude the isomorphism (proof lines 19039-19051): combining the vanishing range with the torsion property and the pull-out lemma identifies the two sides; the canonical map is then an isomorphism, which is the stated projection formula.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to stalks and compute the stalk of the right-hand side using commutation of the derived tensor product with pullback.
Record the vanishing range from global dimension one and the torsion property of the coefficients.
Apply the pull-out lemma over Z to identify both sides and finish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the projection formula Rf_*E tensor^L_Z K = Rf_*(E tensor^L_Z f^{-1}K) for a proper morphism and torsion coefficients over Z (statement lines 19000-19010). The proof (proof lines 19012-19051) verifies the canonical map on stalks, where the right-hand side becomes E_x tensor^L_Z K_y, records the vanishing range coming from global dimension one and the torsion property of the tensor complex, and applies the pull-out lemma over the ring of integers to conclude. H2: one stalk computation followed by a pull-out step, written out.
